patterns: Ultra-short 6-15s clips focusing on hyper-specific daily overthinking moments (e.g., cringing at 5-year-old memories)
Relatable social conflict skits depicting exaggerated internal monologues vs. external reality
High-contrast dynamic animation styles (smooth hair movements, fluid facial expressions) that viewers rewatch to admire
Dark humor combined with absurdity (e.g., asserting dominance through bizarre actions) to handle social anxiety
Conversational banter between two distinct characters acting out inner dialogue vs. vocal reality
title_formulas: How to Handle [Awkward Social Situation] Like a Pro
Only [Trait, e.g., Overthinkers/Introverts] Will Understand This...
opening_3s: Mia starts spiraling out loud over a tiny interaction while Leo stares in complete disbelief
Leo freezes mid-sentence as a giant, visual 'overthinking node' explodes behind his head
A rapid-fire zoom onto Mia's eyes showing a 3-second animated flashback of an embarrassing memory
comment_themes: Appreciation for smooth, fluid animation details and unique art styles
Resonating deeply with nighttime overthinking and nostalgia triggers
Humorous reactions to dark/absurd advice for social anxiety
Relating to childhood experiences translating into adult introversion or quietness
avoid: Videos longer than 60 seconds without fast-paced visual gags or heavy editing
Generic motivational advice without an exaggerated humorous skit
Static scenes lacking expressive character movement or fluid animation flexes
try_next: A 12-second clip where Leo tries to explain 'The Spotlight Effect' while Mia thinks everyone in the coffee shop is judging her shoe untying technique
A 7-second snappy animation of Mia going to bed, where her brain presents a slideshow of every wrong name she called someone this year
A 20-second skit showing Leo using 'Cognitive Reframing' to handle a rude comment, while Mia visualizes the absurd, extreme alternative response
